items.title: Mozambique: Finland donates €1M food from Ukraine to Cabo Delgado displaced
items.summary: The Government of Finland on Wednesday donated food to support 330,000 people affected by the armed conflict in the Mozambican province of Cabo Delgado. The initiative, valued at around €1 million, involved the purchase of food products from Ukraine The donation, comprising rice and soya oil, was formally handed over on Wednesday in Pemba, Cabo Delgado, by Finland’s Ambassador to Mozambique, Satu Lassila, to the Cabo Delgado provincial government and the World Food Programme (WFP) On the occasion, the Finnish ambassador expressed concern about the humanitarian situation in the province, which has been affected by attacks by extremist groups for almost a decade “The humanitarian situation in Cabo Delgado is worrying. items.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
items.summary: Watch: Hong Kong pro-democracy advocate Joshua Wong jailed for 10 years Joshua Wong, once the face of Hong Kong's democracy movement, has been sentenced to 10 years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the city's sweeping national security law Wong is among hundreds of campaigners and ordinary Hongkongers arrested under the law, which was imposed in 2020 following explosive pro-democracy protests against Beijing's growing control Critics say the far-reaching law has silenced dissent, but authorities argue that it is needed to maintain stability and deny it has weakened the city's cherished autonomy Having already spent the last six years in jail, Wong, who was due to be freed in January, will now spend another decade behind bars Silenced and erased, Hong Kong's decade of protest is now a defiant memory What a defiant mogul's trial says about Hong Kong Wong, who turned 30 last month, has already been imprisoned multiple times for his activism which started when he was in his early teens On Thursday, he arrived in court wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt, khaki trousers…

items.title: France: More than 600,000 protest as anger grows over cost of living
items.summary: Demonstrators took to the streets in several French cities to call for government action on the high cost of living. Protests were largely peaceful, but there were some reports of escalation, including in Paris Hundreds of thousands of people descended on the streets of French cities on Thursday for a new round of protests over rising cost of living Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the total number of protesters ballooned over the course of the afternoon, from 270,000 to 600,000 by the evening The five unions that organized the protests represent public and private sectors, and are calling on the government to address deteriorating public services and high prices of goods Public and private sector workers were joined by students, who have organized their numerous protests of their own over the course of the past month One of the biggest student protests in October turned violent, with rioters having vandalized stores.

items.title: Government to mobilize about 27 billion meticais for mitigation of El Niño
items.summary: Maputo, 05 Nov (AIM) – The Mozambican government plans to mobilize approximately 27 billion meticais (1.7 billion US dollars at the current exchange rate) to implement the 2026/27 National Plan for Mitigating the Impacts of El Niño weather phenomenon. The plan aims to cover sectors of agriculture, health, education, water supply, food assistance, and social protection sectors. According to the Prime Minister Benvinda Levi, who was speaking on Wednesday at the country’s parliament, Assembly of the Republic, in response to concerns raised by parliamentary groups, the measure is also aimed at distributing agricultural input kits to over 185,000 households, incusing the construction of multi-purpose silos to complement small-scale irrigation systems, and the rehabilitation or construction of dams, water supply systems, and multi-purpose boreholes, “all aimed at benefiting more than one million people.” The 2026/27 rainy season points to normal rainfall in the Northern provinces of Nampula, Cabo Delgado, and Niassa.

items.title: Frelimo Extraordinary Session to take place on November 27-28
items.summary: Maputo, 05 Nov (AIM) – Mozambique’s ruling Frelimo Party has announced that the 5th Extraordinary Session of its Central Committee will take place on November 27–28 at the party’s Central School in Matola city, southern Maputo province. According to the party’s Central Committee spokesperson, Pedro Guiliche – speaking following an Ordinary Session of the Political Commission, which was chaired by the party’s President Daniel Chapo – the party will focus on three main agenda items: the review and approval of the directive on internal elections for party bodies; the Code of Ethical Conduct and Party Discipline; and the theses for the 13th Congress. The approval of these instruments is part of the preparations for the 13th Congress, scheduled to take place from July 20 to 25, 2027, in the northern city of Nampula.

items.title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening
items.summary: Cetirizine is commonly used to relieve allergy symptoms Kenyan pharmacists have warned women against inserting allergy tablets into their vaginas in an attempt to make them tighter, following the spread of potentially dangerous medical advice on social media The warning follows a wave of social media posts promoting cetirizine - a widely available oral antihistamine used to treat allergies - as a way of tightening the vagina, supposedly to enhance sexual pleasure Although antihistamines can sometimes cause dryness as a side effect, experts say this does not strengthen vaginal muscles "Dryness is not tightness... instead, it may increase friction, discomfort, and the risk of tissue injury," the Pharmaceutical Society of Kenya (PSK) said "Inserting oral tablets is unsafe. Cetirizine tablets are made to be swallowed.

items.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
items.summary: More than 500 parties are contesting the elections South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC) This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern.
